items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Well who was with Jack Carey in there? Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd.

ctx.x: That's right, he's on the record with you I think. Yeah, yeah.

I believe. Well who was with Jack Carey in there? Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd. Well I'll tell you about that now. They had a boy, I don't know if he's Kent the Old Man Robichaux or not, but we used to call him Robichaux and he claimed he's a relation to Old Man Robichaux, he played violin at the Larry Theater. He's real light with nice hair. Well he played clarinet with us at the Moes. Played what?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: Well, George Foster, like I said.

ctx.x: Oh, buddy. Now, who are some of the bass players you like really? I mean, seriously, with all the jokes and stuff.
Well, George Foster, like I said. Chester Zardes. Oh, yeah.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: Well, Chester Zottis, George Foster, and Bob Lyons.

ctx.x: He left kind of early too. Who were some of the good bass players down here? Huh? Who were some of the good bass players that played with writing bands?

Uh, bass violins? Uh huh. Chester Boone? Uh huh. Chester Boone? You know him? Chester who? No, Chester Zottis. Yeah. They got a Chester Boone in Houston. Now he's a player, that's all his name, Chester Boone. Well, Chester Zottis, George Foster, and Bob Lyons. Johnny, uh, used to play trombone and got on bass at the day. Was it Johnny?
Who did he play with? He played the Rover Show, yeah.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: We couldn't punch, he didn't have no horn.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, we saw a punch coming. He's got the power. But he don't know his horn. You don't know him, huh? No. You know Guy Kelly? He sounds like- You remember Guy Kelly?

Yeah. Well look, if you see him, you see Guy Kelly, you see him. Look just like him for the world. Guy Kelly worked for him, brother. Yeah, I bought, I had to buy it at what it mean to Lorenzo Stoyle, bought, paid three dollars for a horn out of the pawn shop for a- We couldn't punch, he didn't have no horn. Then he made us mad, we were going to take the horn, but Jack Carey, much Carey's brother, stopped him from taking the horn. I had the hatchet to chop the horn in half. I was going to give Stoyle's his half…
